newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - FINANCIAL TIMES - MAY 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - FINANCIAL TIMES - MAY 15.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
-- ROCK BAND THREATENS TO SUE OVER INTERNET COPYRIGHT

The management of British rock superstars Oasis have threatened that if fans who run Oasis websites do not remove certain material from the sites within 30 days, they will face legal action. There are currently hundreds of websites dedicated to the band containing video and sound clips, as well as song lyrics and photographs which management claim violate copyright laws. Music is one of the most popular areas of the Internet, with thousands of unofficial as well as official sites dedicated to various bands and the Oasis case could set a significant precedent.
-- NEW CAR SALES RISE ON NATIONAL INCENTIVE PLANS

Western European new car registrations rose 9.3 per cent in April 1997 compared with 1996, to about 108,000 units, with sharp increases in Spain and Italy offsetting continued declines in France and Korea. National Incentive schemes such as fiscal incentives in Italy, which counted for almost 75 per cent of all new car sales, have been credited for the rise. In a comparison of car manufacturers, Fiat sales rose 23 per cent, Renault rose 13.4 per cent and Peugeot-Citroen rose 2.2 per cent.
-- RATES FOR EMU COULD BE SET THIS YEAR

Jacques Poos, the current Luxembourg foreign minister has confirmed that exchange rates for countries proposed for Emu entry could be fixed before the end of 1997 in a move to avoid turbulence on the money markets. Luxembourg will wait at least until autumn to make the decision, as it hopes to have a better indication of who will qualifies for the single currency, a decision seen by some as controversial. Poos added that the final decision may be ratified by the European Council or a summit of EU leaders.
-- DOUBTS OVER 1 BILLION STERLING FROM AIRWAVE SALE

Analysts have reacted with doubt towards plans by the Labour government to raise one billion sterling through the sale of radio frequencies, stating major revenues would not arrive before 2000. The main area of difficulty for the government will be that they can only sell blocks of frequency not being used at the moment, and most mobile operators have at least 10 to 20 years before their licenses run out. There is also doubt towards interest in a fifth UK wireless operator. Labour had hoped that the airwaves sale would help compensate for declining revenues in traditional privatisations and have denied that the sale would amount to a "mobile phone tax".
-- EARNINGS GROWTH SLOWS TO 4.5 PER CENT

Despite continuing declines in UK unemployment, it is not expected that interest rates will rise any further due to a slowdown in wage increases in March. The Office of National Statistics released figures showing a March underlying earnings slowdown to 4.5 per cent, on target with Bank of England predictions for meeting the government's 2.5 per cent inflation target. The Bank warned that provided productivity growth continued at around the two per cent mark, underlying earnings growth of over 4.5 per cent "would be unlikely to be consistent with the inflation target".
-- TECHNOLOGY TEACHING 'NEEDS 1 BILLION STERLING BOOST'

Britain's Engineering Council has issued a report which states that if UK schools do not receive a one billion sterling donation for technology teaching, it will be very difficult to maintain the country's international status as a "highly competitive and innovative manufacturing nation". The Council based their announcement on a Brunel University Centre for Education and Employment survey of 344 state secondary schools, which found UK technology teaching to be "bedeviled by underfunding", or schools unable to hire properly qualified technology staff.
-- US UTILITY OWNERS SEEK WINDFALL TAX RELIEF

The nine US owners of UK utilities, such as CalEnergy which owns Nothern Electric, are hoping they will be permitted to claim tax relief in the US on the UK government's proposed windfall tax. Current belief has profit tax on privatised utilities raising between three and five billion sterling, with financial markets predicting electricity sector tax alone to raise 2.5 billion sterling. A city law firm has announced that windfall tax relief would come only if the windfall tax falls within the "class of taxation defined by existing treaty provisions".
-- C&W PROFITS RISE 12 PER CENT TO 1.42 BILLION STERLING

The second largest telecommunications operator in the UK, Cable & Wireless, has announced pre-tax profits up 12 per cent to 1.42 billion sterling and turnover ahead 13 per cent to seven billion sterling due to impressive performances from its Hongkong Telecom and UK operator Mercury businesses. Shares in C&W continue to fall, however, indicating negative reaction to the group's refusal to comment on its position in the future of HkT. The pre-tax figures include losses of 93 million sterling and 42 million sterling from C&W's Vebacom and One 2 One businesses respectively.
-- STRONG POUND HURTS SAGE

Newcastle-based accounting software company Sage Group has recorded first-half profits lower than market expectations, with pre-tax profits of 19.3 million sterling and turnover of 73.6 million sterling. Lack of significant growth in the two areas was blamed on the strength of sterling and the cost of restructuring at its French subsidiaries. Aidan Hughes, the finance director at Sage, said that profits were reduced 1.1 million sterling and sales lowered 5.5 million because of the "adverse" exchange rates.
-- COMPUSERVE TO EXIT INTERNET ACCESS SERVICE

Feeling threatened by the advance of telecoms groups such as British Telecom into the Internet area, CompuServe, the UK's largest online service has announced it will cease offering its Internet services in the UK, US and Germany this autumn. CompuServe has reported losses in the past four quarters and now plans to concentrate on other business, such as offering news to professionals. The company will not sell of its Internet business, but hopes its future customers will come through other Internet service providers.
